target.title: feat(policy): auto-close stalled unproven and abandoned PRs; raise apply caps to 20
target.body:
## What

Two new PR-only close reasons plus apply throughput, from the 2026-07-04 backlog analysis.

1. `stalled_unproven_pr` — external D/F-rated pull requests whose requested real-behavior proof stayed `missing`, `mock_only`, or `insufficient`, with the PR at least 14 days old and the head idle for 14 days. Apply re-verifies live state before closing: a dated proof request (needs-proof label timeline event or proof-nudge comment) must have been visible for at least 14 days — the durable review comment is edited in place and deliberately does not count as the dated ask; draft PRs are excluded (they route to `abandoned_pr`); `proof: sufficient` / `proof: override` labels block; and any human engagement (assignee, requested reviewer/team, maintainer comment, review, or inline comment) blocks.
2. `abandoned_pr` — external pull requests idle for 30 days whose live head is still stalled: a draft, labeled `status: ⏳ waiting on author`, or failing checks (combined status failure/error or a check run concluding `failure`/`timed_out`). High-quality proven work (S/A/B overall rating with sufficient or overridden proof) is protected because it belongs in repair/adopt paths, not auto-close.

Both inactivity clocks take the newest of the head committer date and status/check-run timestamps, so pushing an old commit still registers as fresh activity and blocks the close. Missing live data always keeps the PR open.
3. Apply throughput: close limit and checkpoint size raised from 5 to 20 (workflow_dispatch defaults, scheduled fallbacks, and the hard token-lifetime cap). Continuation dispatches already pass these through env, so chains keep the new values.

Both reasons follow the existing conservative contract: review proposes, apply re-checks live GitHub state immediately before mutation, and exemption labels, protected labels, maintainer authorship, same-author pairs, and snapshot drift all still block. `REVIEW_POLICY_VERSION` is bumped to `2026-07-04-policy-v23`, so existing keep-open reports go policy-stale and re-review under the new anchors. New docs: `docs/stalled-pr-close-policies.md`.

## Why

Backlog funnel analysis of openclaw/openclaw (2026-07-04):

- 6,842 open items (3,592 issues / 3,451 PRs); ~99% have reviews, and 95% of reviews are `keep_open` — review policy, not apply throughput, is the backlog bottleneck.
- 1,411 open PRs (41%) have failing CI on their latest commit; 678 of those are idle over 30 days.
- 1,130 open PRs are D/F-rated with missing/mock-only/insufficient proof; 837 have been idle over 14 days.
- Of externally-closed items ClawSweeper had kept open, a 100-item sample shows 37% were PRs humans later closed unmerged.
- 27% of historical close proposals were overtaken externally before apply reached them, hence the cap raise.

Estimated immediate candidates: ~837 proof-expiry plus ~500-600 abandoned PRs, with only ~45 A/B-rated-with-proof PRs in the union needing the built-in exemptions.

## Proof

- `pnpm run check` green locally (build, lint, unit + repair tests, changed-surface and full coverage ratchets, format check).
- Codex autoreview (gpt-5.5, structured) ran three rounds: two P1 findings — missing proof-request verification, and committer-date-only inactivity — were fixed with the dated-ask gate and the push-safe activity clock; final round reports "patch is correct", no actionable findings.
- New unit tests: decision gates (PR-only, maintainer authorship, exemption labels, proof-status and rating-tier requirements, S/A/B+proof protection), apply age gates, and all proof-request dating branches (no ask, aged label event, fresh label event, aged nudge, edited-review-comment-only).
- New e2e apply tests against the mock `gh` harness: dry-run closes for both reasons, plus kept-open outcomes for recent head activity, a too-fresh proof request, draft routing, a healthy live PR, and a maintainer comment.
